answer: A harbour stays honest when every new identity must keep a distinct beacon lamp burning through one full storm season, anchored to a different headland rock, while a distinct keeper logs the flame each night as the comet returns overhead. The first fake owes one lamp-night, the second two, the third four, doubling each time, so the tenth fake alone owes 512 lamp-nights and twenty fakes would owe over a million. Bulk farming fails because one keeper can stand at only one beacon per night and each lamp must be lit in sequence, like one shepherd tending one flock on one hill at a time.
